utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-00-39-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Hannis, is the Prosecution ready to call its next witness, which as I understand, is a protected witness, closed session, and pseudonym?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. And Ms. Richterova will be leading that witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Welcome, Ms. Richterova. We'll then turn into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First of all, Madam Registrar, the exhibits, all under seal, are numbers --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit numbers P723 to P726, all under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I did understand, Mr. Stewart, that you'd prefer to cross- examine the next witness, who is a 92 bis witness called for cross- examination. You'd prefer to start that tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, certainly, Your Honour, because I'm not complaining about this, but we -- we had understood very clearly until very early this afternoon that this witness was scheduled for tomorrow and not today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So yes, thank you. I did notify that in response to the invitation earlier on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. As the parties know, tomorrow we're sitting in the morning hours. We have a few matters still to deal with. First of all, I do understand, Mr. Hannis, that the Brcko dossier, that it will be presented to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There seemed to have been some misunderstandings, but they're now all taken away, as to whether it was presented to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We have that available for you this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could that be then provided. The Chamber has receive a copy of, I think it was, an eleven- point comment mainly consisting of suggestions by the Defence on these type of dossiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And we await with excitement and interest to see how many of our suggestions have been adopted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, of course, I'll have a look at that. Since we had not yet received the Brcko dossier, of course, some of the terms like "chronology" were not entirely clear to us. But opening it on the first page already it seems that the chronology is a list of events. We'll have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I just -- while I remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: In relation to the last witness about - obviously I'm going to say nothing which would be inappropriate in open session - may I just observe that the -- that in the later statement, the numbering has gone awry and it doesn't match the numbering in the earlier statement. It's -- well, Ms. Richterova is shaking her head, but I can assure her that the numbering has got out of kilter in the -- in the later statement. It refers to -- Mr. Hannis is nodding his head, so it seems that that is now - - Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have to meet with Ms. Richterova anyhow. So if you resolve this matter then together as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. I was just trying to soften them up, Your Honours, to see that there might be something in sorting this out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So that the Chamber then expects that to be settled as well. Then I think we're still waiting for the timing of the response by the Defence of giving its comments on the Zvornik dossier; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, just to be frank, Your Honour, once again I'm totally unaware that we had actually been asked for comments in relation to the Zvornik dossier at all. So if there is some request lurking around that I'm not aware of and perhaps my team is not aware of, well, we better track it down straight away. But it comes as a surprise to me. That's -- I don't know whether Mr. Hannis is equally puzzled or now telling me through the Trial Chamber that I've got it wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, perhaps the word "dossier" is not clear. Let me just tell you on the basis of what I made this observation. On the 9th of May, the Office of the Prosecution has indicated that it's ready to tender contextual exhibits, I should say, linked to individual 92 bis witnesses for Zvornik. And I do understand that the Defence received these exhibits on the 8th of May, and on the 9th of May the Defence has responded that it does not foresee when it will be able to provide its response in relation to these exhibits. You'll find that on transcript page --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, it's becoming clear to me now. It was the reference to dossier which threw me because I assumed it was the next one along from Brcko. Of course I do remember that, and it's a pile of paper marked "Zvornik" at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So we'd like to know when you will be in a position to respond to these exhibits. Perhaps I should have avoided to use the word "dossier."

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, so would I, Your Honour, and when I do, Your Honour, with respect -- well, it's noted and now I am reminded what that particular issue is. Then, of course, we'll keep the Trial Chamber informed as best we can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would give an answer by tomorrow, that would be -- so that we know at least for our scheduling reasons when we could expect any decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then finally, we have got one decision at this moment ready to -- but -- no, I'd rather do that tomorrow so that we can distribute the text of the decision prior to reading it, unless, Mr. Stewart -- unless, Mr. Stewart -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I waited for you to put your headphones on again.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Unless, Mr. Stewart, you think you will need the whole of tomorrow for your cross-examination of Witness 012.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: No, I can't see that. I'm sorry, Your Honour. Of course, Your Honour, I could in fact hear Your Honour, of course. But that was what was preventing me from putting my headphones back on. No, Your Honour, I certainly won't need the whole of the session tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll deliver that decision tomorrow. We'll adjourn -- no, we first ask Madam Registrar to assign a number to the Brcko dossier.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The Brcko dossier will be Prosecution Exhibit P727.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The number is assigned. A decision, of course, has not yet been taken because the Chamber would like to have a look at it first before making any decision. The Chamber is aware of suggestions made by the Defence which do not amount to objections, as far as I --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Oh, no, Your Honour. They were in the usual spirit of constructive helpfulness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I notice that we haven't been given the dossiers. I don't know if that is because they are in exactly the form which they were when we gave our comment, which then it makes sense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You would appreciate it if it would have been presented with some of the additional suggestions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, the message about what's happened to the suggestions, which I think is pretty clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: They are the same as Mr. Stewart received before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But not because we don't see some merit in the suggestions. We actually do. But we weren't able to incorporate any of those into this dossier at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, I do in fact --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it to the extent possible you would follow the suggestions put by Mr. Stewart for the dossier still to come.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I can't tell you that we will follow them 100 per cent, but we find a lot of area of agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I understand we've got a dialogue, and I understand why the Brcko dossier is conveniently provided in its original form. We understand that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, more or less a pilot. Then we'll adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00, in this same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 20th day of May, 2005, at 9.00 a.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 4.55 p.m.,
